reply_text:
I found the quoted words on the page exactly as given, and I read the candidate as a **pass**.

**1. Is the quote on the page?** Yes, word for word. The page is OpenAI's post "Elon Musk wanted an OpenAI for-profit", which prints the 2017 emails in full. Under the heading "Bi-weekly updates" is an email headed "From: Ilya Sutskever… Date: Mon, Jun 12, 2017 at 10:39 PM… To: Greg Brockman, [redacted], Elon Musk". Its "Dota 2" section reads: "We will solve the 1v1 version of the game in 1 month. Fans of the game care about 1v1 a fair bit." The post is OpenAI's own, not a news report, and it reproduces his email in full, so the source counts as his own words.

**2. The four parts of the rule**
- **Part 1, role:** On 2017-06-12 he was co-founder and chief scientist of OpenAI. In this email he reports the company's plans to its backers, so he is the named chief scientist speaking for it. OpenAI then was a research lab that had not yet released a frontier model, but it is on the list of qualifying companies, so this passes.
- **Part 2, forward-looking and about AI:** It says an AI system (OpenAI's Dota 2 bot) will reach a stated ability. It is not a business forecast and is not framed as a hypothetical. Passes.
- **Part 3, date:** "in 1 month" is a span counted from the day it was said. Passes.
- **Part 4, source:** The email itself, printed in full by OpenAI. Passes.
- **Already recorded?** No. None of his five recorded claim files is from 2017 or about Dota.

**Points for the checker:**
- **Words that weren't meant to be public.** The email was private and only published later. The rule doesn't require words to be public, so this doesn't fail it, but it's an unusual source. You may want to rule on it.
- **Is this a goal?** "We will" is a lab director stating an internal plan, so it could be marked `is_goal`.
- **"Solve" isn't defined.** This doesn't affect admission, but the test will need a plain reading of "solve" when the claim is scored.
- **A second candidate in the same email.** The "Robotics" section says: "In 6 months, we will accomplish at least one of: single-handed Rubik's cube, pen spinning, Chinese balls spinning…". It should be checked separately.
- **Lines I would leave out:** "increase the number of our GPUs by a factor of 10x in the next 1–2 months" is a computing build-out forecast, which part 2 excludes. Two lines from 2016 on the same page, "the next 6 to 9 months" (one of them Musk's), predate his email. I didn't read them against the rule.
